evidence_refs.quote: Emergent, a San Francisco, CA-based provider of an AI software creation platform

Emergent is looking to gain a share of this crowded market by targeting entrepreneurs looking to start new businesses and small and medium-sized companies that have traditionally relied on email, spreadsheets, and messaging apps to run their operations.

Emergent provides a platform that allows to create full-stack, production-ready applications using autonomous AI agents, working like full development teams that design, build, test, and scale software end to end.
non-technical users need a platform that handles deployment, hosting, testing, and debugging alongside the work of programming.

Orthogonal ( orthogonal.com ), a YC W26 startup building a unified API and payments layer for AI agents
Orthogonal, a San Francisco, California-based developer of a discovery, orchestration, and payments layer for AI agents
Orthogonal acts as a single gateway that lets agents discover, access, and pay for hundreds of APIs without separate credentials or subscriptions.
Orthogonal offers developers a unified SDK, API, MCP, and CLI that connects agents to internet services through a single integration.

Adapter is making available a developer tool and API, called Adapter Mind, intended for developers and tinkerers to start using immediately to connect to existing applications, and to spin up new ones.

Adapter is the cognition layer for AI. Connect your data — from your life, your business, or your product — and Adapter connects the dots and builds a constantly-improving graph of your world. Ask a hard question and get a nuanced answer with cited sources in seconds.

It’s also shared with test users a consumer-facing harness, called Adapter Life, as an example of a tool that can build upon Adapter to operate like a super-charged chatbot or agentic assistant, communicated with via iMessage or WhatsApp.
Based in Austin, Texas, the startup employs 17 people

San Francisco-based Rime is trying to gain an edge in this crowded market with its voice AI models
Rime has built a recording studio in San Francisco to collect its own conversational data rather than relying on scraping the web for audio.
Rime released Mist v3 in April — a production TTS engine with roughly 40ms p90 time-to-first-byte and deterministic pronunciation control for brand names and medical terminology
Coda, a dual-decoder flagship model shipping with more than 600 voices across 50-plus languages
